context: SE-AUTOMATION-001B identified reproducible read-only engineering operations (health, context reconstruction, task readiness, verification bundle, project consistency, traceability, skill/adapter conformance, checkpoint preparation). AUTO-01 'health' was identified as the first automation to implement: a read-only aggregation of existing health checks (doctor, validate, capabilities --check, review) into a unified health report. The B0 phase (ADR-0022) established the read-only aggregation surface and minimum-context/on-demand policy. AUTO-01 is the first concrete automation to implement on that surface.
problem: Operators currently must manually run multiple commands (se doctor, se validate, se capabilities --check, se review) and mentally aggregate their results to assess system health. This is error-prone, time-consuming, and doesn't produce a machine-readable health summary for downstream consumers (SE-CONSOLE, CI/CD, alerting). A single command should aggregate all health signals into a deterministic, machine-readable health envelope.

options_considered.option: New 'se health' command aggregating existing read-only checks (doctor, validate, capabilities --check, review) into a unified se.report/1 envelope

SE-CONSOLE can consume JSON without becoming authoritative
cons: Requires ADR + command-contract change (COMMANDS/commands.json + adapter regeneration)
Must define health status aggregation logic (PASS/WARN/FAIL/DEGRADED)

pros: Central place for all health logic

decision: Adopt a READ-ONLY HEALTH AGGREGATION COMMAND (AUTO-01) as a small native extension of the reference implementation, governed by the MINIMUM CONTEXT / ON-DEMAND policy from ADR-0022. The command composes existing read-only functions (run_doctor, cmd_validate, check_policies, cmd_review) into a deterministic se.report/1 envelope with operation='health'. It never mutates, never creates records, never bypasses or auto-passes gates, and never grants authority. JSON output is opt-in via --json; default is human-readable summary. No new schema; health status vocabulary is PASS/WARN/FAIL/DEGRADED/UNKNOWN. DEFAULT = smallest sufficient context (aggregated status + summary); broader context requires explicit --scope flag (future). No new engine, no new schema, no new authority.
reason: All health signals are already computable from canonical files by existing read-only functions; composing them behind a stable envelope yields deterministic, auditable, portable output while preserving AUTOMATE OPERATIONS, NOT AUTHORITY and the single-source-of-truth rule. A default-minimum, on-demand scope model directly reduces the context sent to the model without promising any unmeasured savings.
consequences: Implementation in a future authorized phase (after SE-MCP-INTEGRATION-001 completes). Adding the command requires: (1) COMMANDS/commands.json entry for 'health' (CMD-0015), (2) CLI parser update (cli.py), (3) command implementation in commands.py (cmd_health), (4) ADR for the command contract, (5) tests, (6) adapter regeneration. The envelope uses the existing se.report/1 contract (ADR-0022). No new schema; health status vocabulary extends the existing PASS/WARN/FAIL with DEGRADED. B3 (AUTO-07/08) can proceed independently.
